cells.title: Overview
cells.source: Model **ABM-SIM** is Godley and Lavoie Model SIM populated by many households. Each household holds its own money, forms its own disposable income, and has its own propensity to consume. Macro totals emerge by summing over agents. This notebook runs a Monte Carlo of that agent-based model in the browser from a YAML-authored `abm-model` cell. The R reference is `references/leeds_lectures_2026/ABM_SIM.R`.
cells.more:
Aggregate and IO models are **top-down**: they write economy-wide behavioural
rules directly. **Agent-based models (ABMs)** are **bottom-up**: they specify
many individual agents — here households — and obtain macro variables by
_summing over agents_. Aggregate regularities then **emerge** from interaction
rather than being imposed.

Three features distinguish this style:

1. **Heterogeneity.** Each household has its own propensity to consume out of
   income (`alpha1`).
2. **Interaction and matching.** A random **job lottery** (who is hired) and a
   **first-come-first-served** goods market (who gets served when output is short).
3. **Sequential decisions.** Agents act from _last_ period's information, so there
   is no simultaneous equation system to iterate within the period.

The model remains **stock-flow consistent**: money is only transferred between
agents, so household money `H_d` tracks government money supply `H_s` to machine
precision. The ABM is repeated with different random seeds (**Monte Carlo**); charts
show the **mean** across runs.

Mean output still converges toward `G / theta`, as in textbook SIM. With hiring
friction `s > 0`, unemployment emerges, and wealth settles _above_ the frictionless
SIM value because rationing creates involuntary saving.

cells.title: ABM-SIM specification
cells.description: Declarative agent-based SIM: heterogeneous households, job lottery, FCFS goods market. Tick order matches Leeds ABM_SIM.R (`runif` hiring draw before shuffle). Upper-case names are MACRO totals (Monte Carlo means); lower-case / `*_h*` names are MICRO histories from MC run 1 only — the same split as R's `store` vs `cHist`/`eHist`/`hHist`.
cells.more:
**Macro vs micro (Leeds convention).** The R script comments
`upper-case = MACRO total; lower-case = MICRO (one household)`.

- **Macro** (`record.series`): one value per period, averaged across Monte Carlo
  runs — `Y`, `C`, `YD`, `H_d`, `H_s`, `UR`, plus policy/accounting helpers
  `G`, `TAX`, `N`. Banded series also store p10–p90 paths.
- **Micro** (`record.micro`): full period paths for selected households from
  **MC run 1 only** (not averaged). Default probes are the first and last
  household (`c_h1`, `h_hLast`, …). Author `agents: all` with a raised
  `maxAgents` to match R's full population panels.

Stock-flow check: `|H_d - H_s|` must stay within `tolerance` every period.

do: min(min(floor(Nd * runif(1 - s, 1 + s)), floor(Nd)), households.size)

cells.title: Period ticks
cells.source: One period unfolds as the ordered tick list in the ABM-SIM specification above: plan consumption, hire via a job lottery, shuffle the queue, serve government then households first-come-first-served, pay wages and taxes, and update money holdings. Government spending rises from `20` to `30` at period `60`.
cells.more:
Conventions: upper-case = MACRO total; lower-case = one household (MICRO).
Recorded MACRO series are Monte Carlo means; MICRO probes (`c_h1`, `h_hLast`, …)
come from MC run 1 only — see the ABM-SIM specification cell.

1. Each household plans `cd = min(alpha1 * yd + alpha2 * h, h)` using its own
   `alpha1` and last period's disposable income and cash.
2. Aggregate demand is `AD = sum(cd) + G`. Labour needed is `Nd = AD / pr`.
3. Hiring: `N = min(floor(Nd * runif(1-s, 1+s)), floor(Nd), households.size)`.
4. One random shuffle orders both jobs and the shop queue (`households.rank`).
5. Households with `households.rank <= N` are employed (`e = 1`).
6. Government is served first from produced goods `N * pr`; remaining output is
   rationed FCFS to households.
7. Hired households earn wage `w = pr` (zero profit). Taxes `theta * y` are paid;
   money updates as `h = h + y - c - tax`. Money supply grows by `YG - TAX`.

Setting `s = 0` with homogeneous `alpha1` recovers the textbook SIM money stock
`H = (1 - theta) * (G / theta) * (1 - alpha1) / alpha2` in the limit.

cells.title: ABM-SIM balance sheet (MC means)
cells.description: Household money holdings mirror government money liabilities. Cells are linear in the Monte Carlo mean series, so row and column sums remain watertight.

cells.title: ABM-SIM transactions-flow matrix (MC means)
cells.description: Period flows among households, production, and government. Use the period scrubber to inspect a single period after the run.

cells.title: Monte Carlo baseline
cells.description: ABM-SIM Monte Carlo (mean paths). Defaults match the Leeds R script except `monteCarlo: 50` for a snappier browser run (R uses 100).

cells.title: Total output (MC mean)
cells.description: MACRO output `Y` (MC mean with p10–p90 band). Vertical shift at period 60 is the government-spending shock.

cells.title: Disposable income and consumption
cells.description: MACRO means of disposable income `YD` and consumption `C` with p10–p90 bands (R panel b).

cells.title: Money stock
cells.description: MACRO household money `H_d` and government money `H_s` (MC means with p10–p90 bands). With hiring friction, wealth sits above the frictionless SIM benchmark at mean alpha1.

cells.title: Unemployment rate (emergent)
cells.description: MACRO unemployment rate `UR` (MC mean with p10–p90 band). Emerges from the job lottery when hiring friction `s > 0` (R panel d).

cells.title: First household (micro, MC run 1)
cells.description: MICRO paths for household 1 from MC run 1 only (not averaged): consumption `c_h1`, cash `h_h1`, employment `e_h1` (1 when employed). Matches R panel e.

cells.title: Last household (micro, MC run 1)
cells.description: MICRO paths for the last household from MC run 1 only: `c_hLast`, `h_hLast`, `e_hLast`. Matches R panel f — compare with the first household to see heterogeneity and queue order.

cells.title: Baseline variable summary
cells.description: MACRO series summary (MC means). Micro probes `c_h1` / `h_hLast` / … are available on the household charts above.
